tasks.short: Keep attendance, grades and other required student records

steps.what: Maintain student attendance records during the session
Enter student grades in the required course records
Copy grades into other student information records
Check the student information copy against the course record
Publish accepted grades in the student information record
Read mail about attendance records and grades

tasks.design: The engineering teacher still marks attendance in the room and enters the decided grade once in the course record on the {LMS}. A deterministic copy then fills the same student identifier, course code, attempt, grade and date into the {OTHER} student information record. The teacher checks that copy and only then publishes the accepted version; the copy itself is not the release.
tasks.previous_blocker: The two records did not share a grade, so the teacher typed the result a second time.
tasks.enabler_now: Both records already store a student identifier, a course code and a grade, so a copy can fill the second from the first without a model.
tasks.still_hard: The examiner still has to set the result, and a row with no student identifier cannot be guessed.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing who is in the room, and releasing only a result the examiner will stand behind.
tasks.altitude: The second typing of an already decided grade leaves the week. Attendance, the first entry, the check and the publication stay. The teacher does not gain a right to publish an unchecked result.

reach.task: Set which fields a grade record needs
reach.learn: Which student-record fields must be present before a result can be published.

evidence.claim: One university requires a grade kept in the course record to be published as well in the official student record, which is a second entry of the same grade.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set the result.
A grade already stored against a student identifier, a course code, an attempt and a date can be copied into a second record that uses the same fields, with no model.

assumptions: Published means sum to 100. Floors of 20.6, 17.4, 4.9, 35.8 and 21.3 are 20, 17, 4, 35 and 21, which add to 97. The three extras go to mail (remainder 0.9), documents (0.8) and screens (0.6), giving 21, 17, 5, 36 and 21.
This task does not keep a workbook. The 17 spreadsheet points move onto screens. Shares used are screens 38, spreadsheets 0, mail 5, documents 36 and meetings 21.
The document share is the first entry of the decided grade in the course record on the {LMS}. The screen share is the copy (17), the check (16) and the publication (5). There is no paper card.

The copy reads five fields only: student identifier, course code, attempt, grade and date. The producer is the course grade record the teacher enters. A row with no student identifier is not guessed. The teacher types that row on the check, which stays at full time.

The actor on every step is the engineering teacher, including the copy. That person marks attendance, enters the grade, checks the copy and publishes today. The machine appears only as the future fate of the copy.

The first entry in the course record is a plain save and is not gated. The copy is a draft and is not gated. The only release is publication of accepted grade record v1. A later edit voids the check. The publication does not change that version.
Mismatches are typed by the teacher on the check. There is no retry loop. The check compares the grade, the course code, the attempt and the date, not only the identifier.
Exam marking is a different task and is not counted here. The grade is already decided when it is entered.

A native sync between the {LMS} course record and the {OTHER} student information record is tried before custom code. The build days cover a small copy, and access to the student record, only if configuration cannot share those five fields.

The copy is not a view of how the teacher works. It does not score the teacher, so no staff-monitoring consent is opened. Access still needs the institution's permission. Other countries follow their own national rules on who may set a result.
No focal upkeep is included. The field map is system upkeep and does not reduce the net. The check stays at 100 and is already inside that step.

All shares are focal. Central net is 17, the copy step only. Low is a module whose two records do not share a student identifier, so nothing is copied. High leaves about 5 points of the copy for rows with no student identifier. That haircut is an assumption, not a measured fraction. Attendance, the first entry, the check, the publication and the mail stay at full time.
unknowns: Whether this institution keeps a course record and a separate official student record.
Whether those two records already share a student identifier, a course code, an attempt, a grade and a date.
Who may grant access to the student information record.
How often a grade row has no student identifier.
research_questions: Do the course record and the student information record store the same five fields?
Can the two records be configured to share a grade without a separate copy?
What share of grade rows lacks a student identifier?

already_counted.description: The teacher compares the copy with the course record and types any mismatch. That time stays in the check.

incremental.description: A system keeps the field map from the course record to the student information record. That upkeep is not the teacher's time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a module whose course record and student information record do not share a student identifier, so the teacher still types every row. High keeps about 5 points of the 17-point copy for rows with no student identifier. That haircut is an assumption, not a count. Attendance, the first entry, the check, the publication and the mail stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold scheduled office hours to advise students

steps.what: Read students' mail before regularly scheduled office hours
Read the programme documents the question needs
Maintain office hours to advise and assist students

tasks.design: The office hour is already on the calendar. Shortening that hold would shorten the advice, so the hour stays with the engineering teacher. Reading the student's mail in {EMAIL} and the programme documents in {DOCS} before the hour stays as it is. No advice note is drafted and nothing is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: The advice depends on the question the student brings, which is not stored before the hour.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing in the hour is a structured record a copy could fill. The calendar hold is already the schedule.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the student's question and answering it.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher hears the question and decides what to say.
tasks.altitude: The office hour stays the same length. Nothing is taken off the advice, and the teacher gains no right to skip the hour.

reach.task: Advise a student who is choosing a module
reach.learn: How to hear the question before answering it.

evidence.claim: Hearing a student's question and answering it in a scheduled hour is not a field copy, and shortening the calendar hold would shorten the advice.

assumptions: Published means sum to 100. Floors of 0.8, 0.3, 6.2, 10.3 and 82.3 are 0, 0, 6, 10 and 82, which add to 98. The two extras go to screens (remainder 0.8) and then spreadsheets (remainder 0.3, ahead of documents and meetings), giving 1, 1, 6, 10 and 82.

This task does not keep a workbook and does not do the hour on a screen. The 1 screen point and the 1 spreadsheet point move onto the office hour. Shares used are screens 0, spreadsheets 0, mail 6, documents 10 and meetings 84.
A cut that only shortened the calendar hold was weighed and rejected. The hour is already scheduled. Shortening the hold would shorten the advice.
No advice record is invented, and no line is posted. Nothing is drafted and nothing is sent. The live hour is the work, so it is not gated.
The actor on every step is the engineering teacher. No machine step is added.
Students are outside the staff, so the hour is an external conversation. It is not a colleague talk and it is not a record release.
All shares are focal and remain at 100. Central net is 0. The range is 0 to 0. System upkeep is zero because no copy is added.
unknowns: Whether every office hour is already on a shared calendar.
Whether students send the question by mail before they arrive.
Whether the programme rules the question needs sit in {DOCS}.
research_questions: How often does the student name the question in mail before the hour?
Which programme documents does a typical question need?

incremental.description: No copy and no field map are added, so there is no upkeep. The scheduling cut was rejected because the hour is the advice.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The hour, the mail and the programme reading all stay at full time. A shorter calendar hold was rejected because it would shorten the advice. Central net is 0.

tasks.short: Join student recruitment, registration and placement

steps.what: Read programme documents before student registration
Read the student registration in the student information record
Read mail about student recruitment and registration
Participate in student recruitment and placement activities
Decide the student placement from the registration
Record the accepted placement in the student information record

tasks.design: The engineering teacher reads the programme documents in {DOCS}, the student's registration in the {OTHER} student information record, and the recruitment mail in {EMAIL}. The meeting and the placement decision stay with the teacher, because the placement is not a row that exists before that decision. Only the accepted placement is written into the student information record.
tasks.previous_blocker: The placement does not exist as structured data before the teacher decides it in the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: The registration and the programme rules can be read before the meeting. They do not contain the placement.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding which placement this student should take.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher meets the student and stands behind the placement.
tasks.altitude: Recruitment meetings and placement decisions stay at the same length. The teacher writes the accepted placement once and gains no right to let a filter decide it.

reach.learn: Which placement choices the programme actually allows.

evidence.claim: A placement that is decided in the meeting is not a row that can be copied from an earlier record.

assumptions: Published means sum to 100. Floors of 11.3, 5.8, 12.4, 23.5 and 47.1 are 11, 5, 12, 23 and 47, which add to 98. The two extras go to spreadsheets (remainder 0.8) and documents (0.5), giving 11, 6, 12, 24 and 47.
This task does not keep a workbook. The 6 spreadsheet points move onto the placement write, so screens are 17. Shares used are screens 17, spreadsheets 0, mail 12, documents 24 and meetings 47.

A copy of an existing placement was weighed and rejected. The placement does not exist as structured data before the meeting. A filter that ranked applicants was also rejected. The teacher decides the placement.
The read of the {OTHER} student information record is a read of the registration content. It is not an open-by-id stop.

The meeting is the live recruitment and placement conversation with the student. It is not gated. The only release is the later write of accepted placement v1, and that write does not change the accepted version.
The actor on every step is the engineering teacher. No machine step is added.
The shape prior suggested a pre-structured flow. The placement is not pre-structured, so the decision stays manual.
All shares are focal and remain at 100. Central net is 0. The range is 0 to 0. System upkeep is zero because no copy is added.
unknowns: Whether the registration already names a preferred placement.
Whether someone besides the teacher must accept the placement before it is written.
Which placement choices the programme actually allows.
research_questions: Does the registration store a placement before the meeting?
Who else must accept a placement before it is written?

incremental.description: No copy and no applicant filter are added, so there is no upkeep. The placement is decided in the meeting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The reads, the meeting, the placement decision and the record write all stay at full time. A copy was rejected because the placement does not exist before the decision. Central net is 0.

tasks.short: Choose and order textbooks and laboratory equipment

steps.what: Inspect laboratory equipment the course already has
Read catalogues of textbooks and laboratory equipment
Select textbooks, materials, supplies and laboratory equipment
Write the requisition for the selected materials
Obtain the supplies by sending the supplier the order

tasks.design: The engineering teacher inspects the laboratory equipment already in the room and reads catalogues of textbooks and supplies in {DOCS}. The choice of edition and of what the lab still lacks stays with the teacher. The accepted choice is written as a requisition in {PROCUREMENT} and sent to the supplier from {EMAIL}. Neither step changes the choice.
tasks.previous_blocker: The edition and the gap in the laboratory are the selection. Last year's identifier does not decide them.
tasks.enabler_now: The catalogues and the equipment already in the room can be read before the choice. They do not make the choice.
tasks.still_hard: Judging which edition and which missing equipment the course needs.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees the gap in the lab and stands behind the edition.
tasks.altitude: Choosing the edition and the missing equipment stays at the same length. The requisition and the supplier order stay separate and still take their time.

reach.learn: How to match a catalogue item to the gap in the lab.

evidence.claim: Choosing a textbook edition and the laboratory equipment that is missing is the selection. A stored identifier from an earlier year does not make that choice.

assumptions: Published means sum to 100. Floors of 7.8, 4.7, 8.8, 14.5 and 64.2 are 7, 4, 8, 14 and 64, which add to 97. Three extras: screens and mail both have remainder 0.8, so screens take the first, then mail, then spreadsheets (0.7), giving 8, 5, 9, 14 and 64.
This task does not keep a workbook. The 5 spreadsheet points move onto the catalogue reading, so documents are 19. Shares used are screens 8, spreadsheets 0, mail 9, documents 19 and meetings 64.
Copying last year's book identifier was weighed and rejected. The edition and the gap in the laboratory are the selection. A machine choice would skip that judgement.

No paper requisition card is used. The requisition is written in {PROCUREMENT}. The supplier order is a separate mail. Both use accepted materials list v1 and neither edits it. A later edit voids both checks.
The actor on every step is the engineering teacher. No machine step is added.
The inspection and the selection stay at full time because the design does not shorten them.
All shares are focal and remain at 100. Central net is 0. The range is 0 to 0. System upkeep is zero because no copy is added.
unknowns: Whether catalogues for this course live in {DOCS} or only with the supplier.
Whether the requisition in {PROCUREMENT} is enough, or the supplier also needs the mail.
Who else must accept a laboratory order before it is sent.
research_questions: Does the purchasing record already hold the chosen edition before the teacher writes the requisition?
Does the supplier accept the order from the purchasing record alone?

incremental.description: No copy of an earlier identifier is added, so there is no upkeep. The edition and the laboratory gap stay with the teacher.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The inspection, the catalogue reading, the selection, the requisition and the supplier order all stay at full time. Copying an earlier book identifier was rejected because the edition and the laboratory gap are the selection. Central net is 0.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week keeps the same teaching, advising and placement meetings. The second typing of a grade that is already in the course record goes away. The teacher still sets the result, still holds the office hour, and still chooses the books and the laboratory equipment.
skills_to_grow: Check a copied grade row against the course record before publishing it.
Hear the student's question before answering it in the office hour.
Match a catalogue item to the gap found in the laboratory.
role.ambitious_version: The teacher publishes one checked grade list and uses the office hour for the student's question.
